title: THE COST OF MAKING OTHERS CLEAN

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: After that, the priest must wash his clothes and bathe himself with water. He may then come into the camp, but he will be ceremonially unclean till evening. The man who burns it must also wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he too will be unclean till evening. — Num 19:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a striking detail that is easy to miss. The priest and the man who prepared this cleansing sacrifice became themselves unclean in the process. In making provision for others to be cleansed, they took on defilement. Those who served the cleansing of others paid a personal cost.

There is something profound here. The very ones who helped provide purity for the community were temporarily set outside it themselves. It is a picture of how bringing cleansing to others often involves bearing a burden ourselves. Ministry, service, and care for others are rarely without cost to the one who gives.

We see this pattern in many who serve. The parent who bears the mess and exhaustion so a child can thrive. The friend who steps into another's pain to help carry it. The servant of God who takes on burdens so that others might be lifted. Making others clean, whole, or well often means bearing something ourselves.

But how faintly this pictures our Saviour. These men became unclean until evening; Jesus took on far more. He, the sinless one, became sin for us — bearing not a temporary, ceremonial uncleanness, but the full weight of our defilement, so that we might be made clean. The One who was perfectly pure entered our filth and carried it to the cross. He was made unclean, in a sense, so that we could be made holy. What these priests pictured in a small way, Christ fulfilled at infinite cost, and by His sacrifice we are cleansed forever.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you experienced the cost of helping to bring healing to others?
2. Why is serving others rarely without some burden to ourselves?
3. How does Jesus becoming "sin for us" move your heart to worship?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for those who bear burdens so that others can be helped, and far more for Jesus, who took on my defilement to make me clean. Give me a willing heart to serve others at cost, as He served me. Amen.
